 HARTFORD, CT — Just over 32,000 Connecticut residents cast their votes using early voting Wednesday, bringing the total number of in-person early voters to 305,032, according to numbers from Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office.
 The state also has received absentee ballots from 44,514 voters, bringing the total number of votes received 349,546 after 10 days of early voting. 
 Of the 32,011 votes cast Wednesday, registered Democrats cast 13,393. Republicans cast 7,257 and minor party and unaffiliated voters cast 11,361.
 Of the total in-person early voters so far, 151,784 were registered Democrats (49.7% of the total), 57,797 were registered Republicans (18.9%) and 95,451 were either unaffiliated or members of a third party (31.2%).
 Of the 44,514 absentee ballots that have been received, registered Democrats submitted 22,951 (51.5%), Republicans returned 8,131 (18.2%) and the unaffiliated and minor party members returned 13,432 (30.1%).
 Early voting continues in person through Nov. 1. Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.
